Test One Coefficient Against One Value

Source: R/restricted.R
statmod_test.Rd

Tests that one coefficient of a fit equals one value, by Wald's statistic, the likelihood ratio, Rao's score or Terrell's gradient.

Usage

statmod_test(
  fit,
  param,
  coefname,
  value = 0,
  test = wald_test(),
  vcov_type = bayesian_vcov()
)

Arguments

fit

A StatmodFit().

param, coefname

Which coefficient, as in statmod_restrict(): the distribution parameter and the coefficient's name in its equation.

value

The value under the null, a single number. The default is 0, which is the value that a summary reports.

test

A test_statistic object: wald_test() (the default), lr_test(), score_test() or gradient_test(). The first reads the unrestricted fit only; the other three cost one restricted refit. The four are compared at test_statistic. A character string is rejected with an error.

vcov_type

A vcov_method object, the variance that the Wald statistic reads, passed to vcov.StatmodFit(): bayesian_vcov() (the default), frequentist_vcov() or unconditional_vcov(). The conventions are compared at vcov_method.

Value

A StatmodTest().

Details

summary(fit, test =) reports one of the four statistics for the rows of the coefficient tables that can be held (not a row under a kinked penalty, not an aliased one, and none for a model with a structural term), always against zero. This function tests one coefficient against any value, for questions that a summary cannot answer, such as whether a slope is one, whether an elasticity is unity, or whether a coefficient matches a value fixed outside the data.

The statistics, the quantities that they read and their cost are described at statmod_stat_at(). The last three are built on the restricted fit of statmod_restrict(), and inverting one gives the interval of confint.StatmodFit().

Reading one row costs one restricted refit, whereas summary(test =) costs one per row. The function also reads the mode error of the refit, which costs one Hessian of the restricted fit; the Rao score statistic reads that matrix anyway, so that it adds no cost there. The summary and the interval do not read the mode error.

See also

test_statistic for the four statistics, vcov_method for the variance conventions, summary.StatmodFit() for the rows that can be held, against zero, confint.StatmodFit() for the interval that a test inverts.

Examples

set.seed(1)
dd <- data.frame(x = rnorm(200))
dd$y <- rpois(200, exp(0.3 + dd$x))
fit <- statmod(y ~ x, distributions7::poisson_distrib(), dd)
## the summary tests whether the slope is zero; this tests whether it is one
statmod_test(fit, param = "mu", coefname = "x", value = 1, test = lr_test())
#> 
#> 	Likelihood-ratio test on a statmod fit
#> 
#> coefficient:  mu:x
#> X-squared = 1.27,  df = 1,  p-value 0.2597
#> alternative hypothesis: true x is not equal to 1
#> estimate: 1.056
statmod_test(fit, param = "mu", coefname = "x", value = 0, test = lr_test())
#> 
#> 	Likelihood-ratio test on a statmod fit
#> 
#> coefficient:  mu:x
#> X-squared = 471.8,  df = 1,  p-value < 1e-16
#> alternative hypothesis: true x is not equal to 0
#> estimate: 1.056
